newsitem.title: UK: Med/W.African crudes firmer, helped by gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Med/W.African crudes firmer, helped by gas oil.

text.p: Mediterranean and West African crudes were mostly firmer on Tuesday with good buying interest seen for gas oil-rich grades, traders said.
The Russian Urals crude market was assessed balanced with sufficient buying interest to match prompt avails.

A September loading cargo was confirmed bought by an Italian refiner around Dated Brent +80 cents cif Augusta. This compares with trade into Spain on Monday for Sept 18-19 loading Urals at the same level.
Iranian Heavy crude were seen in good supply and thin buying interest saw differentials to Urals slip 10 cents to a discount to Dated Brent of around $1.10/15 cents a barrel.

West African crudes continued to firm. Forcados picked up some impetus from gas oil. Traders said September barrels were mostly sold out and price assessments at around Dated Brent +40 cents were for October supplies.
They said the steep IPE gas oil backwardation to October was limiting some of the effects of gas oil's strength, but expected the gas oil-rich grade to continue to firm amid good demand.
"Gas oil is coming into season so we will see a Forcados/ Bonny light (price) flip over eventually," a trader said.

Meanwhile recent refiner buying from the Mediterranean supported Bonny Light at at a small premium of around three cents to Forcados although some of the prompter cargoes, including Qua Iboe barrels, were at parity.
One trader was seen offering a Sept 27-29 loading Qua Iboe cargo in the low Dated Brent +40 cents range and was expected to trade around that level.
The same trader was reported looking to work a Sept 20-22 Escravos into Spain with discussion for these barrels heard at around Dated Brent +36/37 cents, compared with trade on Friday at +35 cents.
